title: Claim, two by two, one reading
summary: A plain 72px claim (nothing is sent until the record and the domains are right), the four services two by two, unruled, each with one sentence on what it puts in place, the one third-party reading on the three capability pages with its field note, and the projects sentence in this page's form: the status first, then the three named as one destination.

reference.site: GoNimbly's large, few labels; the deliverability note's approved tile voice
reference.borrowed: Big sentence-case names, one line each, nothing tiny.
reference.kelwin: Kit claim, kit reading, kit go-links; no codes, no keys, no opening rows.

motion: entrance: the claim rises (kit), the four cells rise in turn, the reading and the projects line follow.
notes: Coherence pass 2: the projects pointer loses its double colon: “Proposed, to be confirmed: email deliverability, the ICP and signal map, or the CRM blueprint, each bought as a single project →”. Round 9 fix: the label no longer restates the claim ('Order of work'); the orchestration line no longer repeats the specimen's 'your operator can read'; the signal-map line no longer rewords the homepage's 'the live signals that say when'; the cells lost their rules (the runbook is the page's one ruled list); 119 words. Validity's 1 in 6 to be re-verified before launch.
